desc:
Maintain a collection of counters, one per key. A key that is not in the collection has count 0. Each operation is a pair [type, key]:

  • [0, key]: increase the count of key by 1 (a new key starts at 1).
  • [1, key]: decrease the count of key by 1; a key whose count drops to 0 leaves the collection. The key is guaranteed to be present.
  • [2, 0]: report the largest count among all keys, or 0 if the collection is empty.
  • [3, 0]: report the smallest count among the keys in the collection, or 0 if the collection is empty.

Return the reported numbers in the order of the queries. For example ops = [[0,5],[0,5],[0,8],[2,0],[3,0],[1,5],[1,5],[3,0],[1,8],[2,0]] gives [2,1,1,0].

Every operation should run in O(1) (amortised or worst case).
constraints: 1 ≤ key ≤ 10<sup>9</sup> for types 0 and 1; the key field is 0 for types 2 and 3
A decrease is only given for a key currently in the collection
hints: The hard part is the minimum: when the key holding the smallest count changes, how do you find the next smallest one without scanning?

Counts change by exactly 1, so the set of distinct counts that are present is like a sorted chain. Keep one bucket per distinct count, holding the keys that currently have that count, and link the buckets in increasing count order.

Increase: move the key from its bucket (count c) to the next bucket, creating a bucket for c + 1 right after it if the next bucket has another count. Decrease: the same towards the previous bucket. Delete buckets that become empty. Max is the last bucket, min is the first.
editorial: Use a doubly linked list of buckets sorted by count, with sentinel nodes at both ends. Every bucket stores its count and the set of keys with that count; a hash map sends each key to its bucket. Because a counter only ever changes by one, the new bucket of a key is always the neighbour of its current bucket (or a new bucket inserted right there), so the order of the list never needs sorting.

Increase: look at the bucket after the key's bucket; if its count is c + 1 use it, else create one. Add the key there, remove it from the old bucket, and unlink the old bucket when it becomes empty. A new key starts from the head sentinel (count 0). Decrease is symmetric using the previous bucket; if the count would reach 0 the key is simply removed. Max and min queries read the buckets next to the tail and head sentinels. Everything is O(1) per operation.
